title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 618-619): M'_{1,1} is the quotient stack [U_{0,3}/Γ_3], where U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,∞} is the Legendre λ-line and Γ_3 ≅ SL(2,Z/2) ≅ 𝔖_3. Over Q, a point of M'_{1,1} is an 𝔖_3-torsor T (frames of 2-torsion points) with an equivariant map T → U_{0,3}. M_{1,1} = [U_{0,3}/Γ̃_3], where Γ̃_3 is a central extension of 𝔖_3 by μ_2 in which the transpositions lift to elements of order 4. This is the dicyclic group of order 12, Z/3 ⋊ Z/4, a quotient of SL(2,Z), and it acts on U_{0,3} through 𝔖_3. Thus M_{1,1} → M'_{1,1} is the μ_2-gerbe that 'rigidifies away' the automorphism -1.

This page: the lifts to M_{1,1} of a Q-rational point of M'_{1,1} are the Γ̃_3-torsors T̃ lifting T. Equivalently, they are the lifts of the homomorphism Π_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q) → 𝔖_3 defining T to a homomorphism Π_Q → Γ̃_3. This is an embedding problem. Its obstruction is the pull-back to Π_Q of the extension 1 → μ_2 → Γ̃_3 → 𝔖_3 → 1, i.e. a class in H^2(Q, μ_2) ≅ ₂Br(Q).

Case studied: the image of T in U_{0,3} is {-j, -j̄}, where j is a primitive cube root of unity. These are the λ-values with j-invariant 0. The stabiliser of such a point in 𝔖_3 is Z/3, and the Galois orbit is connected.

Grothendieck then translates into the section language. A rational point gives a splitting k: Π_Q → π_1(U_{0,3}/Q) (his 'M_{0,3}'). The map Π_Q → 𝔖_3 is k followed by the projection, and it is trivial iff k lands in M^!_{0,3} = Ker(M_{0,3} → 𝔖_3). Here k is trivial on the index-2 subgroup Π'_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q(√-3)), so the image k(Π_Q) ⊂ 𝔖_3 has order 2.

Next page: the image is {1, σ_∞}, so T is induced from the μ_2-torsor Q(√-3). The preimage of {1, σ_∞} in Γ̃_3 is Z/4. The obstruction therefore becomes the classical embedding problem of Q(√-3) into a cyclic quartic field. Its class is χ∪χ = (-3,-3) = (-1,-3) in Br(Q). Done to the end (not on this page), this class is nonzero: it is ramified at ∞ and at 3, since -3 is not a sum of two squares. So such a rational point of M'_{1,1} over j = 0 does not lift to an elliptic curve over Q.
errors: The transcription reads 'connexe sur Q, donc Π_Q → G_3 est surjectif'. This is inconsistent with the rest of the page: the image of Π_Q in 𝔖_3 is of order 2, as stated at the bottom and on p. 619. Either the word is 'n'est pas surjectif', or Grothendieck slips and corrects himself a few lines later.
No mathematical error otherwise; the computation stops before evaluating the obstruction class (-1,-3), which is nonzero.

ideas.what: Lifting points along the μ_2-gerbe M_{1,1} → M'_{1,1} = [U_{0,3}/𝔖_3] as an embedding problem, with obstruction in ₂Br(Q).
ideas.modern_name: Obstruction to lifting points through a gerbe / rigidification; Brauer class of the residual gerbe
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud (non-abelian cohomology, 1971); for M_{1,1}: Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli rigidification, Antieau–Meier on Br(M_{1,1})

ideas.what: Description of the rational point via a Galois section k: Π_Q → π_1(U_{0,3}); the 𝔖_3-torsor is k composed with the projection, and is trivial iff k lands in the kernel group.
ideas.modern_name: Section-conjecture formalism for tripod / tangential points
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings; La Longue Marche (circulated)

ideas.what: Reduction of the obstruction at j=0 to embedding Q(√-3) into a Z/4-extension, via the preimage Z/4 of {1,σ_∞} in Γ̃_3 = Z/3⋊Z/4.
ideas.modern_name: Cyclic quartic embedding problem, class (a,-1) in Br(Q)

missed.claim: The computation implicitly shows that the gerbe M_{1,1} → [U_{0,3}/𝔖_3] has a Q-point at j=0 with nonzero Brauer obstruction (-1,-3). That is, there is a rational point of the 'Legendre quotient' stack not coming from any elliptic curve over Q. This is a concrete instance of the non-triviality of this μ_2-gerbe, known in the later literature on Br(M_{1,1}) and rigidification.
missed.quote: l'obstruction est, comme il se doit, une extension de Π_Q par μ_2, i.e. un élément de H^2(Q, μ_2) ≃ ₂Br(Q)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: an early hands-on example in the anabelian/section-conjecture setting of how Brauer obstructions appear at orbifold points of M_{1,1}. It is not new as a fact.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard non-abelian-cohomology computation (embedding problem with Brauer obstruction) applied to the orbifold point j=0. It fits the Longue Marche framework, and the phenomenon is known in the later Brauer-group-of-M_{1,1} literature.
transcription_corrections: First line likely 'relèvements à M_{1,1} d'un point de M'_{1,1} rat[ionnel] / Q' rather than 'reliants ; M_{1,1} d'un point de M_{1,1}' réel'.
'G_3' / 'G̃_3' is most likely Grothendieck's script 𝔖_3 / 𝔖̃_3 (symmetric group), consistent with p. 619.
'{-j, -j̄}' denotes λ = -j, -j̄ with j a primitive cube root of unity (the j-invariant-0 points).
The 'surjectif' clause is probably negated ('n'est pas surjectif'), given 'k(Π_Q) ⊂ 𝔖_3 est d'ordre 2'.
Struck phrase: 'dans l'image de Π'_Q' rather than 'Γ'_Q'.
Top-left margin likely 'i.e. surjectiv[ité de Π_Q → 𝔖_3] ... un pt de T(Q̄)'.
Middle-left margin likely 'condit. of rationalité, plus bas'.
